name: Kestrel Crop Tee
description:
A clean, slightly oversized crop tee cut to hit just above the hip, made from a mid-weight cotton-modal blend that drapes softly without clinging. Kestrel is a mid-tier streetwear label with roots in the Tier 3 arts district — their aesthetic is restrained, almost deliberately quiet. The tee comes in a range of muted naturals and urban greys, occasionally punctuated by a seasonal run in a saturated color. The only branding is a small embossed 'K' at the interior neckline. No logo on the outside. The hem is finished with a clean single-needle stitch.

This is the shirt you wear when you've figured out what you like and stopped needing to announce it. It fits well with high-waisted trousers, layered under an open shirt, or alone on a warm night in the upper districts. Kestrel has a quiet following among designers, artists, and the kind of Tier 3 professional who has strong opinions about fabric weight but would never say so at a party.
what_it_says: You have taste that doesn't announce itself. You spent more on this shirt than people realize, and that's exactly how you want it.
story_hooks: Kestrel's cotton-modal supplier is a small collective farm in what was once southern Ontario — they're being pressured by a corponation agricultural subsidiary to sell, and Kestrel's founder is quietly funding resistance efforts.

A limited run of Kestrel Crop Tees in a specific rust-orange colorway became an unintentional identifier for a Tier 3 social movement — now Kestrel's lawyers are trying to figure out how to handle the association without alienating either side.
A character receives a Kestrel tee as a gift from someone who knows them very well — the color chosen says something specific about how the giver sees them.
